claims.text: On a knoll above the channel, builders terraced stone houses, repaired walls and laid new floors and hearths across older ones. Most houses were round or oval, about 3–4 metres across. A few were larger and rectangular.
claims.explanation: The envelope spans samples from different contexts. It does not date every structure or establish continuous occupation throughout the whole range.

support.note: Calibrated outer sample ranges and the field evidence for terracing, superimposition and rebuilding.

support.note: Supports the public geographic reference. Archaeological and historical dates are supported by the other cited sources.

claims.text: The 2006–2007 fieldwork found portions of at least 36 structures, including at least 14 that were complete or nearly complete, and identified 17 hearths or subfloor channels.
claims.explanation: These counts describe excavated features from several episodes. They offer no count of the houses standing in a particular year.

support.note: The total-station plan accumulates walls and features across building episodes.

claims.text: Excavated hearths had passages cut under the floors. At least twelve installations had branched channels. In the rectangular Structure 63, two channels ran from the hearth along the house’s long axis. Structure V included a wall shaft and branches that split repeatedly.
claims.explanation: The site date envelope covers sampled archaeological contexts. The architecture paper gives no separate calendar range for Structure 63. Airflow and heating performance are inferred.

support.note: Compares hearth layouts and discusses the inferred functions of shafts and subfloor channels.
